title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
description: Stranded on Mars with only ingenuity and science. The most technically accurate survival story ever written — and genuinely hilarious.

title: Hidden Figures
author: Margot Lee Shetterly
description: The untold story of the Black women mathematicians who powered America's space race. More technically rigorous than the film.

title: Pale Blue Dot
author: Carl Sagan
description: Sagan's meditation on humanity's place in the cosmos, sparked by a photograph of Earth from 6 billion km away. Changes your perspective permanently.

title: The Right Stuff
author: Tom Wolfe
description: The story of Chuck Yeager, the Mercury Seven, and what it meant to have 'the right stuff'. The definitive account of early American spaceflight.

title: Packing for Mars
author: Mary Roach
description: The funniest science book ever written. What does space actually do to a human body? Mary Roach finds out — no topic is off limits.

title: Endurance: A Year in Space
author: Scott Kelly
description: 340 consecutive days aboard the ISS. Scott Kelly's honest, unfiltered account of what long-duration spaceflight actually feels like.

title: Ignition!
author: John D. Clark
description: The legendary cult classic about rocket propellant chemistry. Brutally funny, deeply technical, and long out-of-print until recently. Essential.

title: An Astronaut's Guide to Life on Earth
author: Chris Hadfield
description: 21 years of preparation for 166 days in space. Hadfield's wisdom on excellence, failure, and staying calm under pressure.

title: Fundamentals of Astrodynamics
author: Bate, Mueller & White
description: The orange Dover paperback. Every aerospace engineer owns a copy. Orbital mechanics from first principles — clear, complete, affordable.

title: The Art of Electronics
author: Horowitz & Hill
description: The definitive electronics reference. Every engineer's desk needs this regardless of discipline. Third edition is the one to get.

title: Space Mission Engineering (SMAD)
author: Wertz, Everett & Puschell
description: The industry bible for space mission analysis and design. If you work in the space sector professionally, this lives on your desk.

title: Spacecraft Systems Engineering
author: Fortescue, Swinerd & Stark
description: The comprehensive European reference for spacecraft design. Used in MSc programmes across ESA member states. Covers everything from attitude control to thermal.

title: Raspberry Pi 5 (4 GB)
author: Raspberry Pi Foundation
description: A serious Linux computer the size of a credit card. Prototype ADCS software, run computer vision, host ground station tools.

title: Hakko FX-888D Soldering Station
author: Hakko
description: The gold standard for PCB work. Temperature-stable down to ±2°C, built to last decades. Buy once, solder forever. The station I use daily.

title: Rigol DS1054Z Oscilloscope
author: Rigol
description: 4-channel, 50 MHz (community-hackable to 100 MHz). Best-value bench instrument available. I2C, SPI and UART decoders included.

title: Saleae Logic Pro 8
author: Saleae
description: The best logic analyzer for debugging embedded systems. Decodes I2C, SPI, UART, CAN and more. Worth every cent if you do embedded work.

title: STM32 Nucleo F401RE
author: STMicroelectronics
description: ARM Cortex-M4 development board with Arduino headers. Same architecture used in many satellite OBCs. Great for sensor and ADCS prototyping.

title: Celestron 8x42 TrailSeeker Binoculars
author: Celestron
description: High-quality ED glass binoculars for stargazing and wildlife. The best upgrade from naked-eye astronomy — takes 10 minutes to learn.

title: Sky-Watcher Heritage 130P
author: Sky-Watcher
description: Compact tabletop Dobsonian that punches well above its price. Stunning views of planets and bright nebulae. Folds flat for storage.

title: Celestron StarSense Explorer DX 130AZ
author: Celestron
description: Uses your smartphone camera to locate 120,000+ objects automatically. The smartest beginner scope available. No star charts required.

title: LEGO International Space Station
author: LEGO
description: 864 pieces with rotating solar panels and detachable modules. A desktop showpiece that doubles as a conversation starter.

title: LEGO NASA Apollo Saturn V
author: LEGO
description: One metre tall, 1969 pieces. The best LEGO space set ever made. Every space fan needs this on their shelf.

title: LEGO NASA Mars Rover Perseverance
author: LEGO
description: 1,132 pieces with Ingenuity helicopter, articulated arm, and rocker-bogie suspension that actually works. Stunning detail.

title: LEGO Apollo 11 Lunar Lander
author: LEGO
description: Faithfully reproduced Eagle lander with ascent and descent stages. Includes Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin minifigures.

title: Apollo 13 (Blu-ray)
author: Ron Howard
description: Houston, we have a problem. The true story of mission control saving three astronauts with physics and ingenuity. Technically flawless.

title: Interstellar (4K Ultra HD)
author: Christopher Nolan
description: The most scientifically ambitious space film ever made. Kip Thorne's general relativity rendered at full fidelity. Watch it loud.

title: The Martian (Blu-ray)
author: Ridley Scott
description: Matt Damon survives on Mars with botany and optimism. Faithful to the book, visually stunning. Watch the extended cut.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (4K Blu-ray)
author: Stanley Kubrick
description: The film that defined cinematic space travel. HAL 9000. The monolith. The stargate. Every frame a painting. Mandatory viewing.

title: Hubble Pillars of Creation Art Print
author: NASA / Fine Art Prints
description: The iconic 1995 Hubble image — Eagle Nebula's Pillars of Creation — as a large-format art print. Stunning on any wall.

title: Sega Homestar Flux Star Projector
author: Sega Toys
description: Projects over 60,000 stars onto your ceiling using a real optical lens. A proper home planetarium, not a toy LED lamp.

title: NASA Mission Patch Embroidered Set
author: Collectibles
description: Embroidered patches from Apollo, Space Shuttle, and ISS missions. Frame them, sew them on a jacket, or collect them all.

title: Estes Alpha III Model Rocket Starter Kit
author: Estes
description: The classic intro kit. Includes launcher, igniter, parachute recovery — everything to launch your first rocket. The hobby that starts careers.

title: Estes Interceptor Model Rocket Kit
author: Estes
description: Sleek delta-wing interceptor design. A satisfying build for your second rocket — more assembly, more speed, more impressive launch.

title: Tang Orange Instant Drink
author: Tang
description: The drink of the Gemini astronauts (1965). Retro space fuel. Mix it strong and pretend you are sipping it at zero g.

title: Cocktail Chemistry
author: Nick Fisher
description: Science-meets-bartending: liquid nitrogen, edible stars, galactic colour-changing drinks. Great for space-themed dinner parties.

title: Astronaut Freeze-Dried Ice Cream Sampler
author: Astronaut Foods
description: The real deal — freeze-dried Neapolitan ice cream used in early NASA missions. Crunchy, creamy, and slightly surreal. Perfect gift.

title: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
author: NASA / Delaware North
description: Stand beneath a real Saturn V rocket. Walk inside Space Shuttle Atlantis. The ultimate space pilgrimage — must-do at least once in your life.
